transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, ever since my grandson was killed, something just hasn't been right with me. My daughter can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her, but... I cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore. It's just empty.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of emptiness or sadness in the past, before your grandson passed away?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I'm 84 years old, so of course I've been sad before in my life. You lose people, things happen. But... not this. I've never felt this kind of total emptiness before he died. It's entirely different.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling this empty or low at any other time in your life, even if it was many years ago?

No, like I was just saying, I really haven't. Even going way back to when I was younger, I've never had a period where I felt this empty. I've been through hard times, but nothing at all like this. It really is just since we lost him.
Aside from this feeling of emptiness, have you been feeling unusually restless, worried, or on edge lately?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't really feel restless or worried. Honestly, I don't feel much of anything at all... just that emptiness I mentioned. I'm not on edge or pacing around, I just sort of sit there. So, no, I wouldn't say I've felt that way.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns since this started?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. I mean, I still eat about what I usually do. And my sleep is... well, it's pretty much the same as it always is. I just go to bed and sleep like normal. So, no, my eating and sleeping haven't really been affected by this.
Are there any hobbies, activities, or social interactions that you used to enjoy, but now find that you have no interest in doing?

Yes, there are. I usually go to a walking club with some friends, but I've stopped going to that completely. I just don't have the interest. And... well, my family is depending on me to help plan the funeral repast, but I just cannot bring myself to do it. Those are things I would normally do, but I just can't right now.
Since your grandson's passing, have you found yourself feeling particularly guilty or like you have done something wrong?
No, I don't feel guilty. I know it wasn't my fault, and I haven't done anything wrong. It's just... a terrible thing that happened. But no, I don't have any feelings of guilt about it.
Does this sense of emptiness and loss of interest interfere with your ability to carry out your daily responsibilities or maintain your relationships?

Yes, it really does. Like I mentioned a moment ago, I've completely stopped going to my walking club. And the funeral repast... my family is really depending on me to help plan it, but I just can't bring myself to do it. So, yes, it's definitely getting in the way of my normal responsibilities and being there for the people who need me.
Do you feel like your life has lost its meaning, or that things will never get better for you?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... I've lived a long time, so I know that things do eventually get a little easier to carry, even if it doesn't feel like it today. I don't feel like my life is meaningless. I still have my family, and I know they love me. It's just... a very dark time right now, but I don't believe it will be this bad forever.
Have you found it difficult to focus on things or make simple decisions lately?

No, I haven't really noticed any trouble with that. My mind is still pretty clear. I can focus on things just fine, and making simple decisions hasn't been a problem for me. Like I was saying before, it's more about just not having the heart to do things right now, rather than not being able to concentrate on them. So, no, my focus is okay.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms of anxiety, such as a racing heart, trembling, or feeling physically tense, since your grandson passed away?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. My heart isn't racing, and I'm not shaking or anything. I don't feel particularly tense in my body. It's just... more of a heaviness, really, but not the kind of physical panic or anxiety you're asking about.

Given how much this has impacted your daily life and your ability to help your family, do you feel that your level of distress is significantly more intense than what you would expect to feel when grieving a loved one?

No, I don't think so. I mean... losing a grandson is just an awful, awful thing. I think anyone would be this heartbroken. It's a very heavy sadness, but I wouldn't say it's more intense than what you'd expect for something like this. It just hurts a great deal, which... well, that seems normal to me when someone you love passes away so suddenly.
Since your grandson's passing, have you found yourself thinking about your own death or wishing that your life would end?

No, I haven't. I mean... I know I'm getting up there in years, but I certainly don't wish for my life to end. I haven't been sitting around thinking about my own death or anything like that. I just... I just miss him terribly. But no, I don't want to die myself.
